title.value: Predictive Inference with Feature Conformal Prediction
title.justification: The title succinctly captures the main idea of using feature conformal prediction for predictive inference.
title.quote: P REDICTIVE I NFERENCE WITH F EATURE C ONFORMAL P REDICTION Jiaye Teng1,3,4,∗ , Chuan Wen1,3,4,∗ , Dinghuai Zhang2,∗, Yoshua Bengio2 , Yang Gao1,3,4 , Yang Yuan1,3,4,†

extractions.description: This paper discusses an advancement in conformal prediction, extending it to the feature space in deep learning for better predictive inference. The study demonstrates theoretical and empirical improvements in efficiency and uncertainty quantification in various tasks, including image segmentation and classification, while ensuring coverage reliability.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on advancements in uncertainty quantification and predictive inference using feature spaces in machine learning, without a specific focus on climate change issues.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this paper, we propose feature conformal prediction, which extends the scope of conformal prediction to semantic feature spaces by leveraging the inductive bias of deep representation learning.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily addresses machine learning concepts and does not directly lend itself to any specific climate change theme or category.
primary_category.quote: Our approach could be combined with not only vanilla conformal prediction, but also other adaptive conformal prediction methods. Apart from experiments on existing predictive inference benchmarks, we also demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of the proposed methods on large-scale tasks such as ImageNet classification and Cityscapes image segmentation.

primary_sub_category.justification: The main focus of the paper is on machine learning methodologies rather than applications or categories related specifically to climate change.
primary_sub_category.quote: From a theoretical perspective, we demonstrate that feature conformal prediction provably outperforms regular conformal prediction under mild assumptions.

new_primary_category.justification: The study's focus is not specifically on climate change; it covers advanced methods in computational predictive inference.
new_primary_category.quote: Our contributions can be summarized as follows: • We propose Feature CP, together with a corresponding non-conformity score and an uncertainty band estimation method.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Since the paper does not address climate change directly, there's no new sub-category applicable here.
